claims.claim: Counts may be truncated to {0,1,2} without losing any information relevant to level-3 restoration.
claims.evidence: For all nonnegative integers a,b, h(a+b)=h(a)⊕h(b) and h(ab)=h(a)⊗h(b), where h(r)=min(2,r). Thus h is a semiring homomorphism. Transfer-matrix counts use only nonnegative sums and products, so saturation preserves exactly the distinctions zero, one, and at least two. Equality to one at each nested uniqueness test is therefore preserved.
claims.witness: The invariant is h(r)=0 iff r=0, h(r)=1 iff r=1, and h(r)=2 iff r≥2; subsequent nonnegative additions and multiplications cannot require distinctions among values already at least two.
claims.search_method: Proved both saturated-semiring identities by integer case analysis, derived their preservation through transfer products, and checked the identities and complete level-3 evaluations with exact integers.

claims.claim: Level-3 additive restoration is decidable in O(m n^3) time under the source paper’s complexity convention.
claims.evidence: For fixed type-3 and type-2 assignments, induction over columns proves that q_i(c) is the saturated number of type-1 prefixes ending with carry c. For fixed type-3 assignments, a second induction proves that d_i(q) is the saturated number of type-2 prefixes producing first-level state q. Consequently, summing d_m(q) over states with q(alpha)=1 tests exactly whether one type-2 assignment has exactly one type-1 completion. Existential choices of local type-3 digits then form ordinary layered reachability. There are 9 q-states and 3^9 d-states. Each column has only three cells, so enumerating all combined local assignments costs at most n^3; all state factors are constants. This gives O(m n^3) under the source convention that regards its O(nm) routines as polynomial. The checker found no mismatch against literal quantifier evaluation.
claims.witness: Exact comparison covered all 31,500 base-2 instances with one or two columns and both final carries, all 432 one-column base-3 instances, and 2,000 seeded instances over bases 2–4 with up to four columns.
claims.search_method: Independently proved both transfer invariants, counted the state and local-enumeration costs, and compared the construction with direct evaluation of ∃v3∃!v2∃!v1 using integer-only exhaustive and seeded checks.

claims.claim: The requested classification is polynomial time; under polynomial-time many-one reductions it is formally P-complete.
claims.evidence: Membership in P follows from claim 1. The language is nontrivial. For any L in P, a polynomial-time reduction can decide its input and output a fixed YES instance or fixed NO instance, proving P-hardness under polynomial-time many-one reductions. Hence the stated formal P-completeness is correct. This is nevertheless a vacuous completeness convention for nontrivial languages in P and supplies no meaningful matching hardness classification under a more restrictive reduction such as logspace.
claims.witness: In base 2 with one column and required final carry 0, [type-3 x]+0=0 is YES by choosing x=0. The instance [type-3 x]+1=0 is NO: x=0 gives the wrong result digit, while x=1 produces forbidden final carry 1. Both were checked literally and by transfer.
claims.search_method: Constructed explicit fixed YES/NO instances and proved the generic decide-and-map polynomial-time reduction for every language in P.

claims.claim: The same construction places every fixed-level additive restoration problem in P.
claims.evidence: Inductively, suppose a deterministic N-state automaton recognizes the predicate remaining after lower types have been eliminated. Eliminating the next globally unique type replaces a state by its vector in {0,1,2}^N of saturated assignment counts. Local transitions sum over that type’s local digit assignments, and acceptance tests whether the saturated total over accepting old states is one. The semiring invariant proves exact nested-uniqueness semantics. The new automaton has at most 3^N states. Starting from the two carry states and repeating for each inner type yields, for every fixed level k, a finite tower-sized state set depending only on k. The outer existential type is handled by layered reachability. Because a column still has at most three variable cells, local enumeration remains at most n^3 times a k-dependent constant.
claims.witness: The inductive state bound is N_0=2 and N_{j+1}≤3^{N_j}; for fixed k this is independent of m and n.
claims.search_method: Proved the automaton-lifting construction by induction on the number of eliminated uniqueness quantifiers; used the exact level-3 checker as a finite validation of the first two lifts.

target_evidence: The exact target requires both a complete upper bound and a matching hardness classification at meaningful strength. The draft correctly proves a substantive polynomial-time upper bound, and even the stronger fixed-level membership result. Its only hardness argument, however, decides an arbitrary P language inside a polynomial-time reduction and selects fixed YES/NO outputs. That makes every nontrivial language in P formally P-complete and does not distinguish the restoration problem within P. The draft expressly concedes that it establishes no standard logspace-reduction P-hardness, yet labels this coarse observation the requested classification and claims FULL resolution. Thus the upper-bound work is valid, but the requested matching/tight lower-bound classification remains absent and the asserted coverage is overstated.
